sentences.text: Avalonnectes was a small rhomaleosaurid plesiosaur distinguished by possessing only 18 to 19 dorsal vertebrae, a low number unique among its relatives.
This animal is considered one of the oldest known plesiosaurs because its fossils represent the earliest occurrence of the group.
The genus was named by Benson, Evans, and Druckenmiller in 2012, combining 'Avalon' from King Arthur legends with the Greek word for 'swimmer'.
The species name 'arturi' honors paleontologist Arthur Cruickshank, who began restudying British Lower Jurassic plesiosaurs in the 1990s.
The holotype specimen NHMUK 14550 includes the back of a skull and a nearly complete, articulated postcranial skeleton preserved in three dimensions.
Fossils were collected at Street in Somerset from the Pre-Planorbis beds of the Blue Lias Formation.
Phylogenetic analysis suggests Avalonnectes is a basal member of the rhomaleosaurid family.
Estimates place the animal's existence between 199.6 and 198 million years ago, while other records suggest a span from 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago during the Hettangian stage.
